correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the coupling in quantile coordinates for atomless states, verifies strict monotonicity, obtains the exact pre-map W_1 cancellation, applies the derivative bound on T, and uses a contraction mapping for the fixed quantile. The two-sided equilibrium constants follow by solving the same fixed-point increment inequality on both sides before cellwise integration. Ordered particle ranks are exactly i/N under the lower-rank convention, and the transient estimate follows from a one-step cellwise W_1 inequality and a geometric recurrence. Bi-Lipschitz resource quantiles make the fixed quantile bi-Lipschitz, justifying absolute continuity. No numerical or partial-enumeration evidence is used as a substitute for an infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source treats homogeneous resources and proves contraction and finite-particle bounds only for the uniform target. Direct full-text comparison found no nonuniform-resource theorem and its stated lower finite-size constant omits the fixed-point denominator recovered here. A general review supplies the surrounding self-consistent-operator framework but not this quantile-targeted finite-size law. Multiple statement-level searches for target quantiles, arbitrary resource laws, resource quantization and finite-particle equilibria found no equivalent or stronger result. The residual folklore risk is recorded rather than treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The replacement of the uniform target by an arbitrary fixed quantile is algebraically natural, so specialists may regard part of the extension as implicit folklore even though no matching statement was located.
The literature comparison was targeted rather than exhaustive across all rank-based interacting-particle fields; an equivalent theorem under different terminology could exist.
No originality claim is made for the underlying one-dimensional monotone-rearrangement identities themselves; originality is assessed for the combined dynamical and finite-size theorem.

value.rationale: Nonuniform resource supply is a natural structural variation of the motivating resource-allocation model, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem identifies the target law’s intrinsic one-dimensional quantization error as the exact finite-size scale, preserves a resource-independent contraction rate, and sharpens the lower equilibrium constant even in the original homogeneous setting. This gives a reusable way to separate microscopic contraction from resource discretization and supplies finite-N information not contained in the homogeneous source theorem.
